jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Geotechnical Stability of Coastal Dikes - DTU Sustain
jobs.description:
Are you interested in starting your research career by contributing to the reduction of flooding risks associated with coastal dike instabilities?

Join DTU Sustain as a PhD candidate and perform pioneering research in slope stability, uncertainty characterisation and risk predictions.

As a PhD student, you will investigate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment of dikes, accounting for uncertainties in soil characterisation through modelling. The project offers a unique opportunity to work with slope stability analysis, statistical methods, physical modelling and risk assessment while addressing one of the pressing challenges of climate change in the built environment. 

You will become part of an ambitious and highly interdisciplinary research environment at DTU Sustain, collaborating closely with the Center for Coasts and Climate Adaptation, The Danish Environmental Protection Agency (formerly Danish Coastal Directorate) and Ghent University, while benefiting from access to state-of-the-art facilities in soil mechanics, geotechnical engineering and physical modelling. The position also includes international research stays with our collaborators, providing opportunities to develop a broad scientific network and gain hands-on experience with complementary expertise and facilities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate you will be responsible for developing, validating and implementing computational tools for the stability assessment in collaboration with team members, supervisors and international collaborators.

In detail your responsibilities will include:

• Implement and benchmark simplified limit equilibrium methods against advanced computational modelling for dike instabilities
• Assess the reliability of simplified and advanced slope stability methods
• Characterise and map the uncertainty of the soil conditions in coastal dikes
• Evaluate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment
• Publish high-quality research in leading international journals and present findings at international conferences.
• Contribute to courses and assist in co-supervision of MSc and BSc students
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be based on the material they submit and one or two stages of interview, online and/or in person. 

The assessment of applications will be ongoing and will start before the application deadline.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. The desired start date is 1 April 2027 depending on academic approval.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Varvara Zania, vaza@dtu.dk

You can read more about the Department of Environmental and Resource Engineering at www.sustain.dtu.dk/en/

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 14 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree, but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

jobs.occupation: Semiconductor process specialists - thin film deposition, plasma etching and characterisation - DTU Nanolab
jobs.description:
DTU Nanolab is looking for experienced engineers and physicists within thin film deposition, thin film plasma etching and thin film characterization in its ISO 4 & 5 cleanroom for micro- and nanofabrication.

We are seeking process specialists for the process specialist team. The team is responsible for thin-film deposition equipment (PVD, CVD, thermal processing), plasma etching systems, and a large suite of characterization tools (AFM, SEM, XRD, XPS, EDX, optical and stylus profilers, ellipsometers, reflectometers, PL mappers, and more). Responsibilities span the full equipment lifecycle, from procurement and implementation to documentation, maintenance, troubleshooting and the development of in-depth tool and process expertise needed to support users throughout a system's lifetime. 

The job
We are seeking people with experience and interest in plasma etching (ICP, IBE), plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD), AFM, sputter deposition, RTP annealing, PE-ALD, XRD and photo spectrometry. The job includes

• Process development of new processes and maintenance of current processes
• Documentation, including user manuals and process documentation
• In charge of QC and calibration procedures 
• Helping, training and education of users
• Assisting in fault finding in cooperation with technicians
• Assisting in procurement of new equipment: Specifications, demo runs and run-in
• Networking with other cleanroom labs in Europe
You will work closely with other process specialists and technicians in the Process Group, as well as with other DTU Nanolab groups, researchers, students and engineers from DTU and commercial companies. A large part of your working day will be spent in ISO 4 and 5 cleanrooms, where you will wear a full cleanroom suit.

Our expectations of you
You must have a M.Sc. or Ph.D. degree within either engineering or physics within a relevant field (micro/nanofabrication, experimental physics or similar) and have knowledge and experimental skills within the area of either plasma etching or thin film deposition and within different relevant characterization tools. 

Furthermore, we expect you to possess skills and qualifications in one or more of these areas:

• Plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD) and other CVD techniques (ALD and LPCVD)
• Plasma etching (ICP etching)
• PVD techniques (sputter deposition, e-beam evaporation and thermal evaporation)
• Thermal processing (oxidation, annealing and rapid thermal annealing)
• Thin film characterization techniques (AFM, XRD, photo spectrometry and other relevant)
• Hands-on experience working in a cleanroom environment
• Have a broad understanding of micro and nano processing
• Have an eye for detail and work meticulously
• Work well in teams with people from different backgrounds
• Service-minded
• Self-driven and able to plan your own working day
• Communicate well in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
At DTU Nanolab, safety is a top priority, and we are looking for candidates who can thrive in a highly safety-conscious environment and meet the following physical and mental requirements: Is able to work in an environment where it can be necessary to wear specialized safety and protective equipment. Is able to respond quickly and effectively in emergency situations, including evacuation in case of alarms. Is able to perform tasks that require work while standing up and mobility for longer periods.

What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international work environment. The work is highly hands-on and with a large degree of variation. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. Please note that this is not a research position, but a technical position, with a main focus to facilitate academic and industrial users within the field of thin film processing and characterization.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

Application and contact

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 April 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Re-advertisement: Multi-physics modelling of wetting–drying induced ground movement, landslides and coastal erosion

Research area and project description
We are looking for a motivated and talented PhD candidate to join our multidisciplinary research team investigating climate-driven geohazards affecting infrastructure and the built environment. The successful candidate will become part of the long-term Villum Foundation research programme Civil Engineering and the Green Transition in the Built Environment (CEBE), bringing together researchers in geotechnical, structural, coastal and environmental engineering.

The PhD project focuses on developing a multi-physics platform to simulate the coupled hydromechanical behaviour of soil interacting with water in a geotechnical context. The overall objective is to establish a combination of numerical methods under the umbrella of multi-physics modelling to assess the stability of slopes and embankments subjected to wetting–drying cycles, changes in groundwater level and saturation, surface erosion from stormwater and debris, and toe erosion from waves in coastal environments.

The integrated modelling tool should describe the onset of slope instability, accounting for different hydroclimatic triggering factors (including variations induced by climate change scenarios), and the evolution of mass movement, considering large deformation. Therefore, different numerical methods may be combined, leveraging on the advantages of each approach for simulating a specific phase of the process. It is not the intent to develop new constitutive models for specific soil types, but it may be relevant to explore the use of meso-scale models for soils such as till and fissured clays, both native to Denmark. However, while the main application should be Danish soils, the numerical framework should be developed with versatility in mind to allow the assessment of climate-driven geohazards generally in urban and coastal regions.

Project description 
Applicants should submit a short research proposal (maximum 4 000 keystrokes) that demonstrates their understanding of the scientific challenge, identifies key knowledge gaps, formulates research objectives and hypotheses, outlines a possible methodological approach, and explains why their background makes them well-suited for the project. The proposal will be refined together with the supervisors during the PhD.

Qualifications and specific competences

The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Methods for design of biobased building enclosure systems with a regenerative environmental impact

Research area and project description
The objective of this Ph.D. project is to define methods for design of building enclosure systems following a paradigm for obtaining a regenerative environmental impact. The project aims to define a gated process for design of such systems and demonstrate its operationalisation in the actual development of building systems in collaboration with producers and companies in the building industry.

The methodological approach will be a combination of co-creation techniques where the Ph.D. student actively engages with the building industry to develop practical and useful design methods and workflows that leads to a regenerative environmental performance of building systems. The work is centered around the use of biobased materials in systems with longevity in terms of building physics. Concepts of circularity is expected to be a lever for this.

The background for the project is that the planetary boundaries are overstepped due to excessive environmental load from human activities which means that humanity has entered a zone of risk of deleterious or even catastrophic environmental change at continental to global scales. The main driver for this is the built environment that e.g. accounts for approx. 43% of all energy-related CO2-emissions. There is therefore an acute need to reduce the environmental load from the built environment to a level that enables the regenerative properties of the planetary ecosystems to reestablish the safe operating space below the planetary boundaries.

Qualifications and specific competences
The candidate must have a technical background in building science such as B.Sc. or B.Eng. or similar. Applicants must furthermore have a technical master’s degree or at least one year of master’s degree in building science, environmental performance of buildings or similar topics. Documented skills in application of life-cycle assessments for buildings, hygrothermal performance simulations, and computer programming is mandatory. Experience in heat and moisture measurements in relation to buildings is preferred but not required.

jobs.description:
SDU Mechanical Engineering (SDU ME), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for an 18-month postdoctoral position in thermodynamics-based whole-ship energy modelling. The position is expected to start in March 2027, with the specific start date to be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

 

What we offer

You will join a research project titled Thermodynamics-Based Whole-Ship Energy Mapping for Retrofit-Oriented Maritime Decarbonization (STERN) funded by Den Danske Maritime Fond. STERN addresses a practical maritime engineering challenge: improvements to individual components do not necessarily result in optimal energy performance for the vessel as a whole. The project will develop physically consistent steady-state and dynamic energy models to quantify interactions among propulsion, auxiliary equipment, cooling and heating systems, waste heat and energy storage under representative operating conditions.

The postdoc will work within an interdisciplinary SDU team led by Assistant Professor Baris Burak Kanbur, together with Professor Marie Lützen and Associate Professor Paride Gullo, and collaborate with maritime partners including the shipping company Hafnia, DESMI and Fredericia Maskinmesterskole (FMS). ShippingLab will support maritime knowledge exchange and outreach. The position offers opportunities for independent scientific development, high-quality publications and close interaction with industry.

 

Main research activities

• 
Develop modular steady-state thermodynamic and energy-balance models for whole-ship energy mapping, covering fuel input, propulsion, auxiliary power, thermal loads, heat rejection and recoverable energy streams.

• 
Extend these models to dynamic energy simulations representing time-varying engine loads, operational profiles, mode transitions and relevant subsystem interactions.

• 
Model and analyze selected marine subsystems and energy-integration pathways, including propulsion-related energy demand, waste heat recovery, HVAC, cooling/heating optimization, thermal storage and battery storage.

• 
Use representative vessel and component data, engineering correlations and partner feedback to check model assumptions, quantify uncertainty and compare baseline and retrofit-oriented scenarios in terms of energy use and emissions.

• 
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, project meetings, reporting and dissemination of non-confidential results.

 

Required qualifications

• 
A PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Thermal Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline (completed by the date of employment).

• 
A strong foundation in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics (thermo-fluids) and energy-system analysis.

• 
Demonstrated experience in numerical thermodynamic or energy-system modelling, including steady-state analysis and time-dependent/dynamic simulation.

• 
Programming or modelling skills in MATLAB, Python or comparable scientific computing environments, with the ability to develop and document reproducible models.

• 
Knowledge of waste heat recovery, refrigeration/HVAC, cooling and heating networks, energy storage or component performance maps.

• 
Ability to conduct independent research, work with an interdisciplinary team and communicate research results effectively in English.

 

Qualifications considered an advantage

• 
Experience with marine engines, propulsion systems, ship energy systems or vessel operating profiles.

• 
Experience with dynamic simulation and control environment like MATLAB Simulink, Modelica/Dymola or equivalent modelling frameworks can also be considered.

• 
Knowledge of advanced control engineering, optimization or model-based control approaches, and experience collaborating with industrial partners.

 

Workplace description 

The position is full-time at SDU ME and located at the SDU main campus in Odense. SDU Odense is the university’s largest campus and provides a strong framework for interdisciplinary research, teaching, and innovation. You will be part of a modern workplace with high professionalism, strong academic communities, and a commitment to diversity and equal opportunities. SDU also offers dedicated support for International Staff. Learn more about careers and work life at SDU here: Careers at SDU.

SDU ME is part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME) at the Faculty of Engineering. The research activities at SDU ME span widely from fluid mechanics, multi-physics simulation and optimization to condition monitoring and structural dynamics, composite materials, mechanical design, and naval architecture and marine engineering. 

The research environment combines thermo-fluid science, energy engineering and computational modelling, with collaboration across SDU and external maritime partners. The successful candidate will contribute to an industry-informed research project while working closely with academic colleagues and maritime experts. The research group is also part of the broader maritime research community at SDU, providing opportunities for transdisciplinary collaboration across faculties through the SDU Maritime Centre.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Odense.

Assessment and selection process

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.

What we offer

be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Software Technology is research and education in software engineering, interactive technology and artificial intelligence. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and interactive software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense and Sønderborg and with the new centre also in Vejle.
